# The Cycles of the World

## The wheel of bloom and rot

> status: ratified (D-0040)

The world had more craft and prosperity in the past and lost it — more than once. It
moves through cycles: some ages grow and innovate sustainably; some grow by devouring
and collapse. The present empire is not the first calamity; it is this cycle's
instance of an old disease. See [[prosperous-cycles]] and the era ladder in
`data/timeline.yaml`.

## Hidden knowledge, staged revelation

> status: ratified (D-0040)

This is not common knowledge. The protagonist discovers it across the story — one
buried stratum, one impossible artifact at a time — and it transforms her pedagogy
from salvage into seed-planting. The narrator, centuries on, understands the cycles
fully but never states them bluntly: the truth is dripped out, an oblique revelation
about the many possible rhythms of human history.

## Agency turns the wheel

> status: ratified (D-0022, D-0040)

The thematic point of the cycles: they are not fate. Individual human agency — 
concretely, the central party: the three and the wolf-spirit — is the worked example
of how a rot-cycle gets bent toward a bloom. The long arc of the story is the endless
work of rebuilding: new societies in the ruins, new ways to live without poisonous
extraction. Hope in this world is a practice, not a prophecy.

## Trauma runs in fractals

> status: ratified (D-0041)

The cycles echo across scales: what the world does in millennia, a society does in
generations, and a person does in a life. The empire is itself a trauma-response
calcified into policy; the trio's private wounds (hypervigilance, cynicism,
dissociation) are the same shape smaller. Healing runs on one mechanism at every
scale: enough safety, enough truth, enough time — the story's echoes are deliberate.

## The stratigraphy

> status: provisional (D-0072)

Approved directionally: the evidence is physical and layered. Bogs preserve the
strata of prior ages ([[megaliths-and-leys]]); dig deep enough and the anchor's spade
strikes woven fibers that do not rot and glassy stones etched too finely for any
living craft. The standing circles are palimpsests — the present stones raised on the
footings of far older works. The world is a layered cake of endings, and the trio
walk on all of them.
